About home backup power in Kenya

KPLC outages can last minutes or a whole day. A home backup power station stores electricity in a battery and switches your essentials over to it, so the fridge keeps cold, the Wi-Fi stays up and the lights stay on — without the noise, fuel and fumes of a petrol generator.

Read moreShow less

Size it by what you want to run and for how long: add up the watts of your essentials and compare them with the station's capacity (Wh) and AC output (W). Our power station sizing guide walks through it, and solar generator pairings show which panels recharge each station during the day. Browse every power station or compare models on our comparison page.

Every unit is genuine and covered by a 24-month warranty. Pay by M-Pesa, card or cash on delivery, with same-day delivery in Nairobi and delivery to all 47 counties with an eTIMS invoice.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best power backup for a home in Kenya?

For most homes, a portable power station: it needs no installation, runs silently with no fuel, and recharges from the wall or solar panels. Choose its size by what you want to keep running during a KPLC outage; the sections above group our stations by home size.

How long will home backup last during a blackout?

Roughly capacity × 0.85 ÷ the watts you use. The BLUETTI AC180P (1,440 Wh) runs a 150 W fridge for approximately 8 hours on its own; adding a TV and lights shortens that. Send us your appliance list on WhatsApp and we will estimate it for you.

Can I add solar to my home backup?

Yes. Most of our power stations accept solar panels, so they recharge during the day without KPLC power. Check the station's solar input and choose panels within it; see our solar generator pairings for matched examples.

Is there a warranty, and how do I pay?

Every unit is genuine and covered by a 24-month warranty. Pay by M-Pesa, card or cash on delivery, with same-day delivery in Nairobi and delivery to all 47 counties with an eTIMS invoice.
